chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who has dirhams (a debt) owed to me, and he sells wine and pigs with them, then pays off the debt from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem,' or said: 'Take it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay off a debt with money earned from selling wine or pigs?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the impurity (najis) or non-halal nature of the source funds—specifically wine and pork—does not invalidate the settlement of a monetary debt, as the creditor receives the value rather than the specific substance. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the purity of the object itself and the validity of the financial transaction, ensuring that creditors are not penalized for the debtor's choice of liquidation assets. It underscores the practical flexibility in commercial law, prioritizing the fulfillment of obligation over the ritual purity of the currency's origin.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man upon whom were Dirhams (as a debt) for me. So he sells wine and pigs, then fulfils from it (clears the debt)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’, or said: ‘Take it (your money)’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who owed me a certain amount of dirham with which he sold wine and pigs and with such business he paid me back. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful’ or that he (the Imam) said, ‘You can take it.’”
